title: Treaty of Versailles
key_facts: Peace treaty that officially ended World War I
Signed on June 28, 1919, in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles
Imposed harsh terms on Germany including war guilt clause and reparations
Created League of Nations as international peacekeeping body
causes: Allied desire for revenge and security against German aggression
Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points and idealistic vision for peace
French demands for security and compensation for war damages
British balancing act between punishment and stability
outcome: Germany accepted terms under protest but never ratified in spirit
Massive reparations burden crippled German economy
Redrew European map and created new nations from former empires
League of Nations established without US participation

figures.name: Woodrow Wilson
figures.role: US President; architect of Fourteen Points

figures.name: Georges Clemenceau
figures.role: French Prime Minister; demanded harsh terms

impacts: Created economic and political conditions that led to World War II
Established principle of war crimes and international law
Redefined European borders and created new nation-states
Set precedent for international cooperation through League of Nations
